subject: BeaconHealth: intermittent path anomalies causing latency and 5xx errors
body:
From: Ops Team <ops@beaconhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: cto@beaconhealth.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent high latency and 500s from Patient API (region-us-east)

Hi Markus / Redwood team,

We started seeing intermittent spikes in latency for the Patient API around 08:50 PST and a series of 500 responses. The spikes correlate with some long tail requests to your inference endpoint. We attached a short tcpdump and the dashboard screenshot. This is impacting background sync jobs and some patient-facing features.

Observed:
- 08:50–09:05 PST: 2–3x p95 latency (200ms -> ~700ms)
- 09:02 PST: burst of 500 responses (~12 requests in 3 minutes)
- Requests cross multiple availability zones; most client IPs are from our VPC in us-east-1

We suspect a network path issue — possibly a VPC peering flap, DNS resolution change, or an intermediate proxy. Can you confirm? This is currently P1 for us.

Thanks,
Dana Mills
Ops Lead, BeaconHealth
Attachment: beaconcall-trace-20270618.txt (tcpdump excerpt)

---
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Ops Team <ops@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent high latency and 500s from Patient API (region-us-east)

Dana — thanks for the quick heads up and trace. I’ve opened a priority incident (INC-4729) and looping in our network lead and CS. Initial read: the packet trace shows asymmetric ACK paths and a few TCP retransmits around the same timestamps.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Marissa will run a controlled trace from our egress and the inference front-door to check for split-handoffs.
- Vivek / infra will look at routing tables for the peered VPCs and any recent firewall rule changes.
- We’ll validate whether any resolver/TTL changes were pushed for the model endpoint.

I’ll schedule a short bridge in 20 minutes to sync.

— Markus Klein
Head of Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | markus_klein@redwood.ai

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent high latency and 500s from Patient API (region-us-east)

Quick update from active probes:
- Confirmed intermittent amplification between our NAT gateway and BeaconHealth's peered subnet (us-east-1a -> us-east-1c).
- DNS lookups for the inference endpoint returned two A records; one addresses to an older front-door that should have been decommissioned last week. TTLs were low (30s) but we see some clients still hitting the stale address.
- Firewall logs show a spike in "established" sessions from a small beacon IP range; some sessions matched an older stateful NAT mapping and triggered TCP RSTs when reflowed.

Hypothesis: a cached DNS/peering route + sticky firewall/NAT sessions -> intermittent asymmetric path that causes retransmits and some 5xx responses when the old front-door drops traffic.

Attaching our internal connection summary pdf.

Marissa
Sr. Network PM, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-internal-conn-summary-0620.pdf

---
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Exec flag: BeaconHealth P1 — ask for SLA tolerance and fallbacks

Vivek — BeaconHealth has classified this P1. The initial on-the-wire evidence suggests sticky NAT/firewall sessions combined with a stale A record in their resolver set; that combination is amplifying latency and returning intermittent 500s.

Customer impact: patient sync jobs delayed, visible errors on web UI. Beacon asked for an exec-level contact and a temporary mitigation plan.

Recommended mitigations (short-term):
1) Push a defensive routing rule to prefer the current front-door IP (force local cache refresh on our edge).
2) Temporarily increase connection timeout and drop threshold on the older front-door so it fails faster (reduce retransmit window).
3) Ask Beacon to flush resolver caches and their load balancer ARP/NAT entries; provide them a simple command set.

Please advise whether we can commit to a 90-minute mitigation window. If yes I’ll propose that to the Beacon CTO and coordinate an hourly update cadence.

— Markus

---
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec flag: BeaconHealth P1 — ask for SLA tolerance and fallbacks

Markus / Marissa — agreed to the mitigation plan. Operational notes:
- I authorized a temporary routing override on the edge fabric to steer traffic away from the deprecated front-door IP at 16:15 PST; override will auto-revert in 4 hours unless we extend.
- Infra will reduce accept timeouts on the old host so it responds with immediate TCP RST rather than stalling client connections.
- Monica: please coordinate the CSM update messages and the exec sync with Beacon CTO at 17:00 PST.

Marissa — follow up with a brief runbook we can send to Beacon for cache/NAT flush steps (keep commands for common OSes and their LB appliances).

We’ll keep the incident open and provide hourly updates until stabilized.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability, Redwood Inference
